conviction_note: Spire is in a live offer period under a recommended FINAL 250p cash offer from Tulip UK Bidco (Toscafund/THCP/Ares), with irrevocables over 53.4% of issued capital, the scheme document published 29 Sep, and a Takeover Panel Rule 4.2(c) ruling barring any revision; spot 245.5p has closed between 245.0p and 246.5p every session since 7 Sep. So the interims (due by 30 Sep under the issuer's own notice) cannot re-rate the shares whatever they show, the reaction function vetoes any print-driven move, and the signed expectation is 0 with an absolute move of a few tenths of a percent.

findings.finding: Spire trades as a merger-arbitrage target pinned 1.8% below a FINAL 250p cash offer that the Panel has barred Bidco from revising (Rule 4.2(c)), with 53.4% of issued capital irrevocably committed and the scheme document out on 29 Sep, so the interims carry no price-relevant information for this window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Since the 7 Sep firm-offer day (close 245.0p) the stock has closed at 245.0-246.5p on every one of 16 sessions, including the 11 Sep Rule 4.2(c) ruling and the 29 Sep scheme document; the pre-bid results reactions in the baseline (median 2.4%) are from a different regime and do not apply.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced, and that is the finding: a stock whose results were not priced would not have held within a 1.5p range for sixteen sessions. What the baseline's lean (+1.2 from the short register) and event_move_proxy (2.4%) assume is a free-floating equity; both are artefacts here.

outside_window.finding: Court Meeting and General Meeting on 30 Oct 2026 need 75% of scheme votes cast; irrevocables cover 42.7% of scheme shares, so the vote, not the interims, is where the remaining 1.8% spread resolves
FCA change-in-control approval for regulated Spire entities is a condition of the scheme; timing unannounced
